points.description: Sets up a usable framework (e.g. coordinates with BC as x-axis, D = foot of altitude from A at origin, A=(0,a), B=(-b,0), C=(c,0)) and correctly finds H=(0,bc/a) and P=(0,-bc/a) (or equivalently shows P lies on the circumcircle / DH=DP with the needed lengths). A synthetic approach that correctly sets up a key auxiliary object (e.g. antipode of B in (ABC) or antipode of A in (AFP)) with a correct relation also earns this credit.

levels.says: Setup is stated but H or P is wrong or only partly justified, or an auxiliary point is constructed with no proven property.

points.description: Uses that A and P lie on the circle (AFP) and both lie on the line AD perpendicular to BC, to get the circle's equation or a relation, e.g. x²+y²+ux+vy+w=0 with v=-(a-bc/a), w=-bc (intersection with the axis x=0 gives y=a and y=-bc/a). Equivalent: the power of D with respect to the circle equals -DA·DP = -bc.

Uses F on line AB with CF⟂AB to get BF·BA = BD·BC (from A,F,D,C concyclic, or by direct computation of F) and equates it to the power of B with respect to circle (AFP), i.e. b(b+c). Equivalent direct verification that F lies on the circle also earns this.

levels.says: Correct idea of power of the point B (or the cyclic quadrilateral AFDC) but the computation or sign is wrong or incomplete.

points.description: Solves for the remaining parameter: u=-2c (i.e. the circle's centre projects to C on BC; equivalently the circle meets BC where x²-2cx-bc=0).

Concludes: the x-coordinates of X and Y are the roots of x²-2cx-bc=0 (discriminant positive as X,Y distinct), so their sum is 2c and the midpoint is x=c, i.e. C. Equivalent: the centre's foot on BC is C, so C is the midpoint of chord XY.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a complete valid proof; any correct alternative (synthetic with antipodes, trigonometric, etc.) earns the corresponding marks. Partial credit is given for the correct setup, the circle through A and P, and the power-of-a-point step for F. Only constructing an auxiliary point such as an antipode with no further correct progress earns about 1 mark; a claim of the result without justification earns 0.
rubric.answer_key:
Coordinates: D = foot of altitude from A, origin; BC is the x-axis; A=(0,a), B=(-b,0), C=(c,0) with a,b,c>0 (acute triangle). Orthocenter H=(0,bc/a), so P=(0,-bc/a).
Circle (AFP): x²+y²+ux+vy+w=0. Setting x=0 gives y=a and y=-bc/a as roots, so v=-(a-bc/a), w=-bc.
Power of B: since B,F,A are collinear, power = BF·BA = BD·BC (A,F,D,C concyclic by right angles at F and D) = b(b+c). Direct: power of B = b²-ub-bc. So b²-ub-bc=b²+bc, giving u=-2c.
Intersect with y=0: x²-2cx-bc=0. Roots X,Y sum to 2c, so the midpoint has x-coordinate c, which is C. Hence C is the midpoint of XY.
